entities.summary: Alexander surnamed Lychnus (Λύχνος), was an ancient Greek rhetorician and poet. He was a native of Ephesus, from which he is sometimes called Alexander Ephesius, and must have lived shortly before the time of Strabo, who mentions him among the more recent Ephesian authors, and also states that he took a part in the political affairs of his native city. Strabo ascribes to him a history, and poems of a didactic kind, viz. one on astronomy and another on geography, in which he describes the great continents of the world, treating of each in a separate work or book, which, as we learn from other sources, bore the name of the continent of which it contained an account.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Alexander Lychnus was a prominent ancient Greek rhetorician and poet who wrote didactic works on astronomy and geography, providing early accounts of continents. His writings demonstrate regional significance in the ancient world.
